summary: Somerset County, ME: 1910 wood tower replaced by a 12-ft steel lookout in 1919; removed in the 1990s, footings remain on the summit; FFLOS says the steel may be at Bolton Hill.

facts.design: 12-foot steel tower (1919) that replaced a wood tower built in 1910
facts.status_note: Tower removed in the 1990s (1994 or 1996, sources differ); a trail sign and the metal footings of the 1919 tower remain on the summit; the FFLOS record says the steel may be at Bolton Hill HQ east of Waterville, unconfirmed by another source

access.note: Summit is on the Appalachian Trail, the highest point on the trail between the Kennebec River and Monson

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Central Maine says 1994, Willhite says 1996, and the FFLOS record says only the 1990s. The story gives both 1994 and 1996 and calls the date uncertain.

The FFLOS record says the tower was set down at the Bolton Hill headquarters east of Waterville and may still be there. Central Maine describes the summit footings only, and no other source read names Bolton Hill; the two accounts do not conflict but only the FFLOS record covers the steel's later location.

notes_for_editor: Removal year conflicts (1994 Central Maine, 1996 Willhite, 1990s FFLOS). The Bolton Hill destination rests only on the FFLOS record; two searches turned up nothing on Bolton Hill, and I did not verify the 'east of Waterville' geography. The 1924 watchman death reported in the Forest Lookouts page and the Willhite page is left out of the story as not needed for a visitor's history; it is a sensitive event. The Central Maine article title was not visible in the cache, so the title here is descriptive. Brief record: height 3.7 m matches the 12-foot 1919 tower; agency matches the Weebly header; access 'unknown' is now public (on the AT).
